# Lintaya

> A local-first workspace that connects operational systems and Git providers
> to dashboards, blocks, boards, a guarded HTTP API, and a read-only CLI.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): product scope, local startup, license, and limitations.
- [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md): runtime boundaries, ConnectorType/Connection,
  persistence, secrets, CLI, and future Team boundary.
- [Setup](SETUP.md): configurable local server, vault, backup, and recovery.
- [Documentation index](docs/INDEX.md): user, operator, and contributor guides.

## Build and extend

- [Connector development guide](docs/connectors/DEVELOPMENT_GUIDE.md): manifests,
  schemas, lifecycle, redaction, routes, and tests.
- [Connector contracts](docs/connectors/CONTRACTS.md): shipped provider limits,
  synchronization, cache, configuration, and capabilities.
- [CLI guide](cli/README.md): profiles, TUI, JSON output, completion, and the
  read-only boundary.

## Agent and API boundaries

- `GET /api/health` is a public liveness check.
- `GET /api/ai-context` is public discovery metadata and must never contain
  credentials, private hostnames, user data, or stored configuration.
- `GET /api/openapi.json` describes the HTTP contract; route descriptions do
  not grant permission.
- Most operational routes require `Authorization: Bearer <HQ_TOKEN>` and an
  agent-originated write must include `X-Actor` for audit attribution.
- Use the Action Registry contract for approved actions. Do not infer an action
  from a button, rendered DOM, cached object, or `data-*` attribute.

## Safety

- Never read, copy, commit, upload, or log ignored runtime data, databases,
  vault exports, backups, local settings, or credentials.
- Connector secrets are write-only and must be redacted from responses, logs,
  diagnostics, exports, and prompts.
- Destructive actions require the applicable approval policy; Team and sandboxed
  repository execution are not released features.

Spanish repository orientation: [llms.es.txt](llms.es.txt).
